article.title: Optimizely Supply-Chain Breach Injected Crypto-Clipper and Card-Skimmer Malware Into 178 Organizations' Sites, Including CNN and BBC
article.summary: Attackers exploited an Optimizely Experimentation signup flaw to inject malware into 188 of 1,611 scanned customer JavaScript snippets, Optimizely confirmed.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Optimizely, a web experimentation and personalization platform whose JavaScript snippets are embedded directly into customer websites, confirmed on November 16, 2026, that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to inject malicious code into customer projects, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/optimizely-supply-chain-attack-delivers-malware-to-cnn-fox-news-bbc-salesforce-sites/). Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI identified the campaign, and his analysis, relayed by [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/17/optimizely-vulnerability-malicious-javascript/) and [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/11/17/optimizely-hack-turns-worlds-biggest-websites-into-malware-dispensers/5310448), found malicious JavaScript served to visitors of 178 organizations, among them BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce and GitLab.

## What We Know

Optimizely customers embed a small JavaScript snippet that loads the company's experimentation code directly into visitors' browsers, according to [Malwarebytes](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack). Attackers abused the signup flow for Optimizely's Experimentation product, adding their own code to the "Project JavaScript" field of customer projects, which was then served from Optimizely's own content delivery network, [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/17/optimizely-vulnerability-malicious-javascript/) reported. [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Major-brands-deliver-malware-in-a-supply-chain-attack-11527963.html) added that the payload loaded from the trusted domain cdn.optimizely.com and carried a valid certificate, making it appear legitimate to browsers.

Optimizely issued a statement confirming the incident: "Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered," according to [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/17/optimizely-vulnerability-malicious-javascript/) and [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/11/17/optimizely-hack-turns-worlds-biggest-websites-into-malware-dispensers/5310448).

Helme's team examined 1,611 Optimizely snippets and found 188 carrying malicious code, affecting 178 organizations, both outlets reported. Banks made up the largest single victim group, with 32 organizations affected, according to [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/17/optimizely-vulnerability-malicious-javascript/) and [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer), which also reported technology, retail, streaming, and news/media companies among the organizations hit. Researchers have dubbed the campaign "OPTIMJACK," [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/11/17/optimizely-hack-turns-worlds-biggest-websites-into-malware-dispensers/5310448) reported.

According to Helme, quoted by [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/17/optimizely-vulnerability-malicious-javascript/): "The malware was a multi-purpose kit. It swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attacker's, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and on iPhones and iPads it delivered the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits." [StepSecurity's](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) technical breakdown said the crypto-clipper component held replacement addresses for eight cryptocurrencies and swapped any address that passed the relevant chain's checksum, while the card skimmer intercepted form submissions and checked captured numbers against the Luhn algorithm before transmitting them to the attacker's server. On iPhones, iPads and iPods, the script loaded the Coruna exploit kit, targeting iOS 13 through 17, and DarkSword, targeting iOS 18.x, per the same report.

The BBC's own snippet went from clean at 02:21 UTC on November 16 to injected by 04:21 UTC, with the full malicious payload live by 08:28 UTC, according to matching timelines from [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) and [Malwarebytes](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack). A card-skimming component was added around 13:43 UTC, and the bulk of cleanup took place between roughly 20:40 and 23:11 UTC that day, per [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) and [Malwarebytes](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack). The Register reported that as of 21:52 UTC on November 16, TalkTalk remained the last organization on Helme's list still running infected code, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/11/17/optimizely-hack-turns-worlds-biggest-websites-into-malware-dispensers/5310448).

Attacker wallets had received roughly $7,040 in cryptocurrency by 19:25 UTC on November 16, according to [StepSecurity's](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) tally of the addresses, a figure [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Major-brands-deliver-malware-in-a-supply-chain-attack-11527963.html) independently reported at the same point in the timeline. Named victims beyond those above include HSBC and IKEA, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/11/17/optimizely-hack-turns-worlds-biggest-websites-into-malware-dispensers/5310448) and [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Major-brands-deliver-malware-in-a-supply-chain-attack-11527963.html); Fox News, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/optimizely-supply-chain-attack-delivers-malware-to-cnn-fox-news-bbc-salesforce-sites/) and [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer); and Equifax, according to [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/17/optimizely-vulnerability-malicious-javascript/) and [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Major-brands-deliver-malware-in-a-supply-chain-attack-11527963.html).

Malwarebytes noted that Optimizely's platform runs on roughly 190,000 websites in total, a scale that underscores how a single compromised signup flow could reach so many unrelated organizations at once, according to [Malwarebytes](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/11/cnn-bbc-zoom-and-other-sites-served-malicious-code-in-supply-chain-attack).

## What We Don't Know

Optimizely has not explained how a vulnerability in its account signup flow let attackers write malicious code into customer projects they did not control, [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) reported, calling the underlying mechanism still unexplained. [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Major-brands-deliver-malware-in-a-supply-chain-attack-11527963.html) likewise reported that, as of its writing, Optimizely had not published a list of affected websites or guidance for people who may have been exposed while browsing them. None of the cited sources reported a final, confirmed count of recovered funds or whether law enforcement had opened an investigation.
